Titan Industrial Equipment Inc. - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Titan Industrial Equipment Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There may be a brief pause while we poll for questions. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Titan Industrial Equipment's results for the Q2 2024. Joining me on today's call are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and David Kim, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Titan Industrial Equipment's performance for the Q2. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. First, we've seen robust order intake with strong book-to-bill trends across our core end markets like construction, mining, and agriculture, reflecting diversified demand and strategic positioning. Second, our backlog has expanded meaningfully, offering clear visibility on conversion timelines into revenue over the next 12 to 24 months. Third, the outlook remains constructive for end-market growth in both the near term through 2025 and the medium term out to 2028, fueled by secular trends in automation and electrification. Fourth, we're guiding for operating margin expansion in the coming quarter and full year, supported by mix improvements and efficiency gains. Fifth, total revenue delivered solid year-over-year growth, driven by execution on new equipment and aftermarket strength. And sixth, total order intake accelerated, underscoring momentum in our high-growth segments.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, John. Good morning, everyone. Turning to our financial performance, Titan Industrial Equipment reported $2.85 billion in revenue for the Q2, representing an 8% increase year-over-year. This builds on the momentum from prior periods, with gross margin at 27.8%, driven by favorable product mix and pricing realization. Operating expenses were $750 million, resulting in an operating income of $463 million. Our net income for the quarter was $350 million, or $1.45 per share.

Let me start with total revenue and the year-over-year growth rate. While our prepared remarks here adapt the context to this quarter's results, we saw standout performance amid a resilient industrial landscape. For Q2, total revenue reached $2.85 billion, up 8% from the prior year period. This reflects eighth consecutive quarter of positive growth, powered by backlog conversion, pricing discipline up 4-6% across the board, and market share gains in premium segments. Our book-to-bill held at 1.25x, with backlog providing strong multi-quarter visibility as capex cycles strengthen in automation and electrification.

By segment, new equipment sales, about 62% of revenue, contributed around $1.77 billion, up 10% year-over-year, led by precision machining and stamping presses for reshoring plays in semiconductors and EVs. Aftermarket parts and services, 25% of the mix, delivered $712 million, up 8%, with installed base utilization at 82% thanks to IoT upgrades in our MachineryGuard platform. Systems integration and automation rounded it out at 13%, surging 20% to $368 million on robotic cells and cobot arms for logistics and food processing.

Regionally, the Americas drove 45% with solid gains from CHIPS Act semis and Mexico nearshoring; EMEA at 30% benefited from German auto EV tooling despite energy pressures; and APAC's 25% share grew on China electronics and India manufacturing incentives. This diversified growth, paired with 45% gross margins, positions us well for continued mid-teens expansion.

Next, on total order intake and year-over-year growth. For the quarter, total order intake reached $2.8 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 5% sequentially on an organic basis, excluding minor FX drag. This caps three straight quarters of double-digit gains, lifting our trailing 12-month book-to-bill to 1.15x and backlog to excellent levels for H2 and beyond. Automation and robotics led at 42% of intake, up 28% organically on hyperscaler fabs and data centers; machine tools and precision equipment, 35%, grew 15% on aerospace ramps; material handling, 23%, rose 12% from e-commerce and EV plants. North America dominated at 48%, up 25%; EMEA 12% growth on renewables; APAC 10% with ex-China strength. Our Industry 4.0 focus, with digital twins in 40% of orders, drove 8% ASP uplift and recurring service growth at 25%.

Diving deeper into order intake and book-to-bill trends by end market. Overall Q2 order intake hit $2.8 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 5% sequentially, bringing trailing 12-month to $10.9 billion, with backlog at $7.2 billion for great visibility into late 2024 and 2025. Consolidated book-to-bill was 1.25x, fifth straight quarter above 1.2x, aided by aftermarket at 42% of intake and 1.35x ratio for margin support.

Construction equipment, 45% or $1.26 billion, up 22% YoY, book-to-bill 1.35x on capex from OEMs and rentals amid chip delays for telematics machines. North America 55% share from IIJA highway and data center projects, including 150 autonomous wheel loaders for a Virginia hyperscaler; EMEA up 15% on EU Green Deal rail/ports; APAC down 2% on China property. FlexForce hybrid excavators, slashing fuel 25%, won repeats from Skanska and Vinci; mid-teens FY24 growth expected.

Mining, 25% or $700 million, +12% YoY, 1.20x book-to-bill with battery-electric haul trucks from Nevada. Australia/LatAm 65%, BHP/Antamina for 40 MegaHaul autonomous trucks; NA flat but IRA unlocking electrification. MineOS AI platform lifted win rates 15%; 8-10% FY24 growth with 98% uptime.

Agriculture, 18% or $504 million, +8% YoY, 1.15x on precision ag amid wet weather. NA 60% with AgroSmart autonomous tractors cutting inputs 20% for Deere independents; Brazil +25%, Europe subsidy hit. BioFuel combines for EU mandates; low-double-digits outlook on $180B US farm income.

Other markets, 12% or $336 million, +25% YoY: oil & gas +35% on Permian fracs, power gen +18% on data center gensets. Balanced mix funds $450 million capex; on track for $11.5-12B FY intake.

Now, on backlog value and expected conversion timeline. Total backlog ended Q2 at $2.85 billion, up 28% YoY from $2.22 billion and 12% sequentially from Q1, fifth straight expansion quarter with 1.32x book-to-bill above peer benchmarks. Discrete automation 42% or $1.20 billion, +35% YoY on robotic welding and AGVs for EV battery lines; CNC/precision 28% or $795 million, +22% on CHIPS semis and aero MRO; heavy industrial 18% or $513 million flat YoY but +15% seq on IRA wind towers; process control 12% or $342 million +18% on LNG skids.

Regions: NA 52% $1.48B +32% on reshoring/IIJA, Dayton fab cutting lead times 25%; EMEA 24% $684M +25% on Green Deal; APAC 20% $570M +20% India/SE Asia offsets China; ROW 4% LatAm mining.

Conversion: 55-60% in 12 months, 85-90% in 24. Next 6 months 35-40% or $1.0-1.14B from EV automation/NA infra; 12 months 55-60% $1.57-1.71B CNC/EMEA green; 24 months 85-90% $2.42-2.57B APAC/heavy; beyond 10-15% custom MRO. Digital twin cuts cycles 20%, FlexMod assembly 40% faster, dual-sourcing boosts turns to 4.2x. Ties to electrification 25%, ESG 35%, AI 50% of skids; pricing +4.2% cushions China/aluminum risks. Underpins raised FY24 revenue $4.8-5.0B.

For outlook on end market growth near and medium term. Guiding organic revenue 7-9% FY24, 8-11% FY25, EBITDA margins to 22-24%. Semis/electronics 28% mix +18-22% '24, 15-18% '25 on AI/TSMC; aero/defense 22% +5-7% on Boeing/Spirit; auto 18% flat-+2% EV shift, Mexico +10%; industrial/general mfg 32% 6-8% CHIPS/IIJA. NA 9-11%, Europe 3-5%, APAC 10-12% India/Vietnam pivot. Medium term 9-12% CAGR: renewables 20-25%, e-mobility 12-15%. $150M capex hybrid machines, digital twins; ESG cuts emissions 40%; inventory 5.2x, FCF >110%.

On operating margin guidance. Q2 adjusted at 14.2%, +110bps YoY on pricing/mix. Q3 14.8-15.2%, revenue $2.95-3.05B; gross 28.5-29.0% richer automation mix 42%; OpEx 13.8% SG&A from Machinery 4.0 AI/ERP savings; input/labor tailwinds. NA 16.5%, EMEA 13.0%, APAC 15.8%. FY24 14.7-15.0%, revenue $11.9-12.1B. Supply derisk 85% nearshored, QuantumEdge launch, $420M capex 3x ROI. Pricing 4.5%, $1.2B FCF buffers risks.

We are managing our capital allocation effectively, prioritizing investments in high-growth areas like automation R&D and returning capital to shareholders through buybacks and dividends.

Next, I will hand over to Lisa Patel, COO, for an operational update.

Lisa Patel (COO):
Thank you, Michael. Operationally, we've been focused on improving productivity and efficiency across our global manufacturing facilities. We've rolled out lean manufacturing principles in our key plants, including Dayton and Nevada, achieving 12% productivity gains through kaizen events and 5S methodologies. Data analytics via our central operations dashboard optimizes throughput, reducing scrap rates by 18% in precision machining lines. We're also investing heavily in supply chain resilience, with dual-sourcing for critical components like rare earths and PLCs, cutting lead times 25% and inventory days to 72. This positions us to navigate any lingering disruptions while supporting backlog burns.

And I would like to turn the call over to our CTO, David Kim, for an update on our technology roadmap.

David Kim (CTO):
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to driving innovation and developing cutting-edge solutions for our customers in the industrial equipment space. We're investing aggressively in R&D, allocating over $250 million this year to artificial intelligence, machine learning, and the Internet of Things. Our new AtlasEdge platform for predictive maintenance and Nexus IIoT system are showing promising early results, with 20-30% uptime improvements and 15% order win boosts in pilots for mining and ag. EquipTwin digital simulations and QuantumEdge hybrid CNCs are transforming customer yields and cycle times. We believe these technologies—along with FlexMod standardization and AI toolpath optimization—will reshape the manufacturing landscape, creating significant opportunities for Titan as reshoring and electrification accelerate.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the growth drivers in your digital solutions business?

David Kim (CTO):
Good morning, Alex. Absolutely. Our digital solutions, including platforms like MineOS, AgroSmart, AtlasEdge, Nexus, and MachineryGuard, are key growth engines, now embedded in over 40% of new orders. In mining, MineOS AI predictive maintenance drove 15% win rates and 98% uptime guarantees, pulling through aftermarket. Ag's AgroSmart with RTK GPS and variable-rate tech cuts costs 20%, winning Deere partners. Semi and auto fabs love Nexus for MindSphere-compatible IIoT, yielding 20% uptime gains. We're seeing 25-35% growth here, with service annuities at 35% of revenue, as Industry 4.0 mandates digital twins and edge AI. Early QuantumEdge feedback projects 18% gross margins on EV/aero tooling.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jordan Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for expanding your presence in emerging markets?

John Reynolds (CEO):
Thanks, Jordan. Emerging markets are a priority, representing 20-25% of our mix with strong tailwinds. In APAC ex-China, we're targeting 15-18% growth via partnerships like Larsen & Toubro in India for metro automation and Samsung in SE Asia for display fabs—up 40% in intake. LatAm mining stays steady on copper at $4.50/lb, with Antamina/BHP awards. Brazil ag rebounded 25% on soy, and we're pivoting Vietnam for nearshoring to dodge China risks (5-10% exposure). Localized fabs in Poland/India, PLI incentives, and ESG presses position us for 10-12% regional growth, derisked by dual-sourcing and 85% nearshoring.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Taylor Brooks with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Taylor Brooks (Morgan Stanley):
How are you addressing the skilled labor shortage in the manufacturing sector?

Lisa Patel (COO):
Good question, Taylor. The labor shortage is industry-wide, but our proactive workforce development is yielding results. We've upskilled 2,500 employees in additive manufacturing, AI toolpaths, and cobot programming via partnerships with community colleges and Siemens certification programs, reducing turnover 15%. Upskilling in electric spindles and digital twins supports ESG goals. Productivity tools like AGVs and predictive analytics offset shortages, with 22% downtime cuts in pilots. We're also attracting talent with 3.5% wage growth below ISM average, tied to performance in our 5G factories.

Operator:
[Pause] There are no further questions at this time.

John Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Titan Industrial Equipment. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
